title: European multicenter study on transrectal sonography in children with colorectal diseases (E-ReKiSo)
summary:
In an international context, there is debate as to whether ultrasound via the abdomen can be used to visualize faecal constipation (Vos et al. 2024, DOI: 10.1007/s00247-024-06083-4).  In some countries, imaging of constipation using X-rays is still standard (Bischoff et al. 2018 DOI: 10.1016/j.jpedsurg.2017.09.022), while others reject this completely. For example, there are attempts to measure the muscle structure of the pelvic floor (Sheng et al. 2024 DOI: 10.1007/s00384-024-04769-7) or by measuring the diameter of the rectum.
 
Rectal malformations and their complications pose a particular challenge. Using a short, anonymous (center-specific pseudonym) questionnaire, a multi-center survey is to be established to provide a better database for infants and children undergoing pediatric surgery.  The aim is to prove that ultrasound as a diagnostic imaging tool for constipation can replace conventional X-rays in everyday care.
conditions: Congenital absence, atresia and stenosis of large intestine
